The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,00,000/- due to death of Sri. G.Rahul Reddy in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
2.

That, on 18.10.2018 at about 3.15 a.m. G.Rahul Reddy was proceeding in a Scorpio vehicle bearing registrtion No.PY-01-BT-2905 from Punganur to Bengaluru, on Bengaluru - Chennai NH-75 road, when he reached near Yelachenahalli, Near Volvo factory, at that time driver of Lorry bearing registrtion No.MH-20-DE-1616 going ahead of Scorpio vehicle, suddenly stopped his vehicle without giving any signal or caution, due to which deceased vehicle came into contact with the said lorry, as a result of which, Rahul reddy sustained grievous injuries & died on the way to MVJ hospital, Hoskote.

Thereafter, post mortem was conducted at Government Hospital,
Hosakote and the body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent huge amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and other incidental charges.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
aged about 22 years.

Since his father was suffering from several health issues and ailments, the deceased looking after the business of his father and earning Rs.45,00,000/- per annum in addition to that, he was also earning Rs.5,00,000/- per month i.e., from the business of Smt.Reddamma & Sri.Ramireddy Kalyanamandapam, Agriculture, Sericulture, Sri.Krishna Cold Storage and Rice mill and contributing the entire income towards welfare of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have put to untold misery, pain, shock and mental agony.

4. It is further stated that, the driver of the lorry was the route cause for the above said accident, but in order to escape from the criminal and civil liability taking undue advantage of the shock of inmates of the Scropio vehicle colluding with the police managed to see that case would be registered against the driver of the Scropio vehicle.

The Nandagudi Police have registered the case against the driver of the Scropio vehicle in Cr.No.225/2018 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A)
of IPC.

The respondent No.1 being the owner of the Lorry bearing Registration No. MH-20-DE-1616 is vicariously liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners, since respondent No.1 has insured the said vehicle with the respondent No.2 since policy was in force as on the date of accident, as such the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.1 did not appear before this court, remained absent,
hence he was placed exparte.

The respondent No.2 to 4 have appeared through their respective G.Krishnareddy vs Hussain Shaik on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107984867/
3 counsel.
The respondent No.3 did not file her w ritten statement.
The respondent No.2 and 4 have filed written statements separately.
6. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing registrtion No.MH- 20-DE-1616, however restricted its liability subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the accident was not occurred due to fault of the driver of Lorry and said Lorry is not at all involved in the accident,
falsely implicated in this case.
As per police records the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Scorpio only.
It is also contention of the respondent that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. as on the date of accident.

Further denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
7. In the written statement, the respondent No.4 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

This respondent has issued Private Car Liability only policy, in respect of said Scorpio vehicle bearing registration No.PY-01-BT-2905 and the risk of inmates is not covered under the policy since no premium has been received covering the risk of the inmates by the insurance company.
Hence, it is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.3.
It is further contended that the accident was not occurred due to fault of the driver of Scorpio, police have filed false case against driver of said Scorpio.
The accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry.
It is also contention of the respondent that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.

With all these main grounds,
prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.
8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that, G Rahul Reddy died due to injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 18.10.2018 at about 03.15 a.m.
near Yelachenahalli (Volvo factory) on NH-75 road on Bangalore-Chennai road in between Hoskote - Kolar due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.MH-20/DE-1616 and Scorpio Vehicle bearing No.
PY-01/BT2905 in an actionable negligence?
(Deleted as per the order dated 12.2.2025)
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate and from whom?

9. Earlier, the claim petition was filed against the respondent No.1 to 4.

But after amendment the petitioners have claimed the compensation only from respondent No.1 & 2 and also pleaded that accident was occurred due to sole negligence of the driver of the Lorry bearing No.MH-20-DE-1616.
But there is no deletion of respondent No.3 & 4 from the petition.
Hence, issue No.1 has been deleted and the issue No.1 recasted as under;

1. Whether the petitioners prove that, G Rahul Reddy died due to injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 18.10.2018 at about 03.15 a.m. near Yelachenahalli (Volvo factory) on NH-75 road on Bangalore-Chennai road in between Hoskote - Kolar due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No. MH-20- DE-1616 in an actionable negligence?
10.
In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 during his life time, was examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P23.

In addition to his evidence placed evidence of driver of Scorpio as PW2 and got marked documents as Ex.P24 and Ex.P25.
11.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 examined its Administrative Officer as RW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
Further respondent No.4 examined its Administrative Officer as RW2 and got marked documents as Ex.R3 & Ex.R4.

12. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
13.

The learned counsel for petitioners has relied following citation:
1. 1994 ACJ 1303 in between Mataji Bewa and others V/s. Hemanta Kumar Jens and another.

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India has formulated the principles as under;
i) In the case of composite negligence, the plaintiff/claimant is entitled to sue both or any of the joint tortfeasors and to recover the entire compensation as liability of joint tortfeasors is joint and several.
ii) In the case of composite negligence, apportionment of compensation between two tortfeasors vis-avis the plaintiff/claimant is not permissible.
He can recover at his option whole damages from any of them.
iii) In case all the joint tortfeasors have been impleaded and evidnce is sufficient, it is open to the Court/Tribunal to determine inter se extent of composite negligence of the drivers.

However,
determination of the extent of negligence between the joint tortfeasors is only for the purpose of their inter se liability so that one may recover the sum from the other after making whole of payment to the plaintiff/claimant to the extent it has satisfied the liability of the other.

In case both of them, have been impleaded and the apportionment/extent of their negligence has been determined by the Court/Tribunal in main case, one joint tortfeasor can recover the amount from the other in the execution proceedings.
iv) It would not be appropriate for the Court/Tribunal to determine the extent of composite negligence of the drivers of two vehicles in the absence of impleadment of other joint tortfeasors.
In such a case, impleaded joint tortfeasor should be left, in case he so desires, to sue the other joint tortfeasor in independent proceedings after passing of the decree or award".

14. My findings to the above issues as follows:
Recasted Issue No.1: In the Negative Issue No.2: Does not survive for consideration Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:-
15. It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No. MH-20/DE-1616 the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Rahul Reddy died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.

16. The respondent No.2 has contended that as per the police records the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of deceased Scorpio vehicle and not on the part of the driver of the Lorry bearing registration No. MH-20/DE-1616.
17.
On the other hand, the respondent No.4 contended that, the accident was not occurred due to fault of the driver of Scorpio, police have filed false case against driver of said Scorpio.
The accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry.

18. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.MH-20/DE-1616.
19.
The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Sri.Krishna Reddy got examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit, he has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon the police documents marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
Ex. P1- true copy of the F.I.R. Ex.P2-true copy of FIS,

Ex.P3-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P4-true copy of Police intimation, Ex.P5 - true copy of Spot mahazar, Ex.P6-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P7 -notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P8- true copy of Inquest report, Ex.P9 -true copy of post mortem report and Ex.P10 -true copy of charge sheet.

G.Krishnareddy vs Hussain Shaik on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107984867/
7 20.

On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by Khalid Salam Chasu i.e., driver of lorry bearing registration No.
MH-20/DE-1616, the S.H.O. of Nandagudi police have registered the case against the driver of the scorpio vehicle bearing registrtion No.PY-01-BT-2905 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337 & 304(A) of I.P.C.
21.

Apart from this, on perusal of spot sketch at Ex.P3 & Ex.P5-mahazar show that lorry was going from Kolar towards Hosakote and behind the lorry, car was proceeding, it is evident about involvement of both the vehicles in the accident. Ex.P4 is the police intimation given to the Sub-inspector of police about the accident.

As per the report of the motor vehicle inspector marked at Ex.P6 alleged accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the offending vehicle and rear side of the lorry damaged and front portion of the car was damaged.

Inquest mahazar and PM report marked at Ex.P8 and Ex.P9 go to show that on the history of RTA G.Rahul Reddy had succumbed to the injuries and cause of death was due to haemorrhage and shock as a result of injury to head and chest, vital organs.
All these material documents remained unshaken.

22. Ultimately, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer as per Ex.P10 against the driver of the Scorpio car by name Shafi Saiyad @ Atheaf alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
23.
In this case, the petitioners have disputed the charge sheet and have claimed that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence driving of driver of Lorry bearing No.MH-20-DE-1616.
To prove the contention, they have examined driver of Scorpio bearing registration No.PY-01-BT-2905 as PW2 who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident.

PW2- in his chief examination has stated that on the date of accident lorry bearing No.MH-20-DE-1616 was going ahead of the scorpio vehicle suddenly stopped without giving any signals or precaution to other road users, as a result,
the scorpio vehicle was driving by him behind the lorry came in contact with the said lorry.
As a result G. Rahul reddy had sustained multiple injuries and died on the way to the hospital.
24. In the cross-examination of PW2 has admitted that, the police have filed charge sheet against him.
He saw the lorry from 15 feet distance, lorry and scorpio vehicles were running  k.m. distance from each other.
The accident occurred on 18.10.2018 at about 3.00 to 3.15 a.m. the brake system was good, if applied the brake within 10 to 15 feet, the vehicle can be stopped.
Further continued that at that time, even if he applied the brake, the vehicle could have touched the lorry.
Further denied the suggestion that, if the damages caused to the vehicle can be observed, the vehicle was in the speed of 100 kms.
Further he has stated that he gave the complaint to the police, but they have not taken the complaint from him.
The police have colluded with the driver of the lorry and filed the charge sheet against him.
25. It is relevant to note that, as per the statement of PW2, the scorpio vehicle was proceeding  k.m. distance from the Lorry before accident.
If PW2 could have maintained 1/2 kms distance while driving the Scorpio, why he has not stopped his vehicle immediately when lorry stopped.

From this,
it is clear that, he was not maintaining the proper distance from the lorry, if he had maintained the proper distance, then accident would not have been occurred.

So, it is clear that the driver of the G.Krishnareddy vs Hussain Shaik on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107984867/
8 scorpio car was in the speed of 100 kms while driving his vehicle.
Further, he is one of the tortfeasor so he always protect himself.
Therefore, his evidence would no way helpful to prove the stand of the petitioner.
Except the evidence of PW2, the petitioners have not placed any other evidences to show that accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver Lorry.
26. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 examined its Administrative Officer as RW1.
He has filed his affidavit in lieu of examination in chief, wherein he has reiterated the averments of the written statement.
He has placed authorisation letter and policy at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
In the cross- examination nothing has been culled out from his mouth to prove the stand of the petitioners.
27. Further, the respondent No.4 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW2.

He has deposed in his evidence that this respondent had issued private car "liability only policy' in respect of Mahindra Scorpio vehicle bearing No.PY-01-BT-2905, which primarily covers third-party risks and does not extend to the occupants of a private vehicle unless specifically stated.
The insurance company is not liable for the injuries or death of inmates of the car under such policies unless an additional premium has been paid to cover their risk.
There is no additional premium is paid in respect of the inmates of the Mahindra Scorpio vehicle.
In the cross- examination he has admitted that respondent No.3 driver dashed the lorry from back side.
Further suggested that the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the scorpio car, for which he has stated that falsely filed.
28. On perusal of police documents and evidence of PW1, RW1 & RW2, one thing is clear that the accident took place on NH-75 road.
As per the records, the driver of lorry was going ahead in front of the scorpio car and driver of the car dashed to the lorry from behind.

But, the petitioner has strongly stressing the point that, as on the date of the accident the driver of the lorry was responsible for the accident and stated that though the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the car,
but the charge sheet is not the conclusive proof. Ofcourse the charge sheet is not the conclusive proof, but at the most it has to be considered facts and circumstances of the case.
Further the petitioners have not placed documents to show that driver of the car tried to give complaint and the same has been rejected by the police.

Keeping in mind the above decisions relied by the counsel for the petitioners, I am of the opinion that, in the present case, the evidence and documents placed by the petitioners clearly reflects that due to the negligent act of the driver of the car the accident occurred.
Hence, the petitioners have utterly failed to prove that the driver of the lorry was responsible for the accident.
29. In the light of the discussions held above, I am of the view that, the petitioners have not placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.
Accordingly, I am answering the Recasted Issue No.1 is in the Negative.

ISSUE No.2:
30.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioners.

As already discussed in issue No.1 that the petitioners have failed to establish that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry, as a result, R.Rahul Reddy succumbed to the injuries.
Hence question of awarding compensation does not arise.

9 ISSUE No.3:
31.

In view of above discussions on recated issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners u/s 166 of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of this case, no order as to costs.
Draw award accordingly.

iii) In case all the joint tortfeasors have been impleaded and evidnce is sufficient, it is open to the Court/Tribunal to determine inter se extent of composite negligence of the drivers.
However,
determination of the extent of negligence between the joint tortfeasors is only for the purpose of their inter se liability so that one may recover the sum from the other after making whole of payment to the plaintiff/claimant to the extent it has satisfied the liability of the other.
In case both of them, have been impleaded and the apportionment/extent of their negligence has been determined by the Court/Tribunal in main case, one joint tortfeasor can recover the amount from the other in the execution proceedings.
iv) It would not be appropriate for the Court/Tribunal to determine the extent of composite negligence of the drivers of two vehicles in the absence of impleadment of other joint tortfeasors.

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,00,000/- due to death of Sri. G.Rahul Reddy in a road traffic accident.
The Nandagudi Police have registered the case against the driver of the Scropio vehicle in Cr.No.225/2018 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A)
of IPC.
The respondent No.1 being the owner of the Lorry bearing Registration No. MH-20-DE-1616 is vicariously liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners, since respondent No.1 has insured the said vehicle with the respondent No.2 since policy was in force as on the date of accident, as such the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
